steps.title: Use microdissection microscope
steps.instruction: Perform the entire dissection under a microdissection microscope as described in the methods.

steps.title: Reference brain hemisphere dimensions
steps.instruction: The fixed right‑hemisphere mouse brain measures approximately 1.9 cm in length and 0.6 cm in height (lateral‑medial view).

steps.title: Separate brain hemispheres
steps.instruction: Place the brain on a clean surface with the dorsal side facing up (ventral side down). Using a scalpel, make a sagittal cut along the longitudinal fissure to separate the left and right hemispheres.

steps.title: Extract thalamus
steps.instruction: On the medial side of the hemisphere, hold the tissue steady with forceps, visualize the thalamus, and scoop it out with the scalpel using blunt dissection while respecting region boundaries.

steps.title: Extract hippocampus
steps.instruction: On the medial side, peel the cortex laterally, perpendicular to the midline, using blunt dissection with the scalpel while holding the hippocampus in place with forceps. Then blunt‑dissect the hippocampus medially toward the midline with the scalpel to free it.

steps.title: Extract striatum
steps.instruction: Expose the striatum by first removing the cortex and hippocampus as described above. Incise around the perimeter of the striatum with fine‑tip thumb forceps, then scoop out the striatum with the scalpel following natural tissue separations; striations help differentiate it from cortex.

steps.title: Excise cortex base
steps.instruction: Using the scalpel blade, excise the base of the already dissected cortex.

steps.title: Remove cerebellum base
steps.instruction: Remove the base of the cerebellum from the rest of the brain with a scalpel, following natural separation planes.

steps.title: Excise brainstem
steps.instruction: Excise the brainstem from the midbrain using the scalpel.

steps.title: Excise olfactory bulb
steps.instruction: Excise the olfactory bulb from the forebrain with the scalpel.
